messages.subject: client-side search engine for the Stan manual?

https://github.com/olivernn/lunr.js

-a

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] client-side search engine for the Stan manual?
parts:
I missed this the first time. If we put it up online,
is there a reason not to just use Google site search?

One issue is that Google site search is weak if others
aren't linking into your site. Otherwise, something that'd
do more relevancy-based search using something like TF/IDF
would be better.

I don't know if anyone had any luck translating the manual
to HTML. I'm all for hosting it if the translation's OK.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] client-side search engine for the Stan manual?
parts:
These javascript search engines are potentially more responsive because you can
load a lot of the data into the client in advance. My sense is that with some
of them the experience is akin to doing search within a word document or pdf.

Here's a good example -- try searching the Rust docs. I think you'll understand
what I mean: http://doc.rust-lang.org/std/index.html

Thanks,

-a

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] client-side search engine for the Stan manual?
parts:
On May 29, 2014, at 8:16 PM, Allen Riddell <a...@ariddell.org> wrote:

> These javascript search engines are potentially more responsive because you can
> load a lot of the data into the client in advance. My sense is that with some
> of them the experience is akin to doing search within a word document or pdf.
>
> Here's a good example -- try searching the Rust docs. I think you'll understand
> what I mean: http://doc.rust-lang.org/std/index.html

That's very cool!

I'm curious how they built it. It only matches
exact substring ("test::coll" but not "test coll"),
so they're probably just following the suffix tree.
It's a linear algorithm in theory, but then there's
all the data transfer and tree construction.

Definitely a different purpose than a site search
with Google or a Solr indexing (they refer to that
net wrapper for Lucene in their doc).

- Bob
